Style: The Map page's own map style. Chart is WDP's white map; the choice here leaves every other map of the app on yours.
WdpLook: Off, the page draws the mission as the Mission map and the VR map board do. On, as WDP draws it: STPT 1 and the IP as squares, tasked points as triangles, targets as diamonds; airfields filled with the colour of the side holding them; the bullseye's 30 nm rings; your side's tankers in dash-dot boxes with their times on station.
LabelInk: The ink of the airfield and navaid names (WDP's Text color). Auto writes dark on Chart and light on the other styles; ONC is the aeronautical chart's purple.
Borders: Country borders and names, as on every map of the app.
Provinces: Provinces and governorates, as on every map of the app.
Towns: Which towns are named: press to step through Off, Mission, Cities, Cities and towns and All places.
Grid: A latitude and longitude grid, from the theater's own coordinates: whole degrees with 10' ticks, and 10' lines once you zoom in. Greyed where the theater's coordinates are not known.
Bullseye: The bullseye with rings every 20 nm, as every map draws it; with WDP's look (or Extra lines) WDP's rings every 30 nm to 150, labelled on the four axes, with spokes every 30°. The bullseye is the save's (the middle of its cell).
ExtraLines: Adds dashed rings every 10 nm and dashed spokes at 10° and 20°.
CursorBullseye: Adds the bearing and range from the bullseye to the pointer: in the readout strip, and beside the cursor on a PC.
Airports: Every airbase of the theater, as every map draws it: a small green ring with its runways (your departure, arrival and alternate larger and named). With WDP's look, filled with the colour of the side holding it now in the save (blue your side, red the enemy, grey neutral). Point at one for its frequencies, TACAN and runways; click it for its card and charts.
Airstrips: The airstrips and highway strips too. Carriers are not drawn here: they move.
AirportLabels: How an airfield is named: its name with elevation, TACAN and approach frequency, its ICAO code, or not at all (the start, as on every map: only your own fields are named). Falcon BMS publishes no IATA codes.
Vortac: The theater's VORTACs with their channel. A click offers to tune the cartridge's TACAN to one.
MaxRange: Each VORTAC's range as a ring, as the theater's data gives it. The ring under the pointer fills.
Viewing: What the flight plan shows: what the jet flies (the cartridge's point where it has one, else BMS's route), the cartridge's points alone, or the mission file's route alone, read only.
SavedLamp: Red while this page or the DTC page has edits Save to DTC has not written; green once they are saved. The Save to DTC button is in the Planner's toolbar.
Stpt: Your flight plan, as every map draws it: rings, targets as diamonds, no leg between a refuel point and a landing, the leg on to the alternate thin and dashed. With WDP's look, STPT 1 and the IP as squares and tasked points as triangles.
TrkDist: Each leg's true track and length in nm at its middle (WDP's Trk/Dist). Legs to or from a landing are left out.
TrkDistMin: Legs shorter than this are not labelled.
Ppt: The cartridge's PPTs: red rings, filled at Circle fill, as the HSD will show them.
PptNumbers: Adds each PPT's number to its label (SA-2/56).
Lines: The cartridge's lines L1-L4, dashed as the HSD draws them, with a dot at each point.
NavOffsets: The attack's nav offsets (VIP or VRP, the pull-up point, OA1 and OA2), laid out from their steerpoints as the jet lays them out.
Tankers: Your side's tankers on station, in boxes 30,000 ft either side of the station leg, labelled with the TACAN a receiver dials (with WDP's look, dash-dot and with the time on station). Your package's own support is always shown.
Awacs: The AWACS of your side as well.
OnStationOnly: Only the tankers on station while your flight is in the air (WDP's rule). Off: every one the save plans.
Package: Another flight of your package: its route in grey-blue with its numbers and callsign.
JstarLamp: Green while a JSTARS of your side is on station at the save's time. Hostile units inside its 200 nm count as seen.
JstarArea: The JSTARS's station and its 200 nm area in magenta.
Types: The air-defence systems the save holds on each side, with how many (and how many your side has seen). Untick a system to take its rings off every layer; kept per theater.
TypesSide: The enemy's systems, or your own side's (WDP's OPFOR and NATO tabs).
TypesAll: Every system of this side on.
TypesNone: Every system of this side off.
Threats: The mission's air defences, as every map of the mission rings them: the sites the printed briefing names (when the flight open is the one BMS printed), else the ones your side has spotted whose ring reaches your route. Yellow rings, dashed until the DTC holds them. The ring is the theater's Ppt.ini range, else the threat reference's.
AllThreats: Every enemy air defence your side knows of (WDP's own Threats layer): spotted, seen recently, or inside a JSTARS's area, with a working radar or none. What your side has not seen is never shown.
Search: Enemy and neutral search radars that still work, as WDP's 'S' rings. 25 nm is WDP's own figure: Falcon BMS publishes no search-radar range and its Ppt.ini has no search type.
SearchLarge: Draws the search rings three times as large (75 nm), as WDP's S Large.
NoRadar: Enemy SAM sites your side knows of whose radar vehicles are destroyed: green dashed rings. Guns and systems with a radar on every launcher are left out.
OwnSams: Your own side's air defence: blue rings.
OwnSearch: Your own side's search radars: purple dotted rings.
Ships: Task forces your side knows of as hull symbols, and while BMS flies the ships the Tacview feed reports.
CircleFill: How strongly the rings are filled (WDP's slider; 20 at the start, as every map fills them): PPTs, threats, own-side SAMs, the VORTAC under the pointer; the JSTARS area at half; with WDP's look, your side's tanker boxes.
AutoPpt: WDP's Auto PPT: PPT 56-70 filled with the threat rings the map draws that have a Ppt.ini type; with more than fifteen, the big ones nearest your route. Asks before it replaces a PPT that holds a point.
ClearPpt: Empties all fifteen PPTs, after asking when any holds a point. Save to DTC writes it.
AddCrossing: Puts the rings your route crosses into the free PPTs, replacing nothing.
RefreshIntel: Asks the PC for the save's intel again (after BMS has saved the campaign).
Line: What this line of your cartridge holds: the mission's name for it, hand-drawn, or empty. Press it to see the line on the map.
ChangeArea: WDP's Change Area: each line kept, cleared, or laid along a tanker or AWACS track, their orbit boxes, the CAP station or a stretch of the route.
ClearLines: Empties the four lines, after asking when any holds points. Save to DTC writes it.
Measure: A ruler: click (or tap) two points for the true and magnetic track and the distance between them. A third click starts again; Esc or a second press of Measure clears it.
SaveMap: Saves the map as it is shown, as a JPEG on the BMS PC: in the flight's DataCards folder when a save's flight is planned, else in the Planner's SavedMaps.
Fit: Back to your flight's area: its route, its support and its PPTs.
Hsd: The HSD preview: the cartridge on black, north up, centred on a steerpoint, at the HSD's own ranges, as the MFD will show it.
Ghosts: On the HSD preview, also what the mission knows and the cartridge does not carry, dim and dashed.
Options: The map's options: layers, intel, tools and lines, as WDP's MAP tab has them.
List: What your HSD will show, and what the mission knows that your DTC does not carry yet.
Readout: Where the pointer is: X and Y (grid km east and north), latitude and longitude, the ground from BMS's height map, the magnetic variation from BMS's own variation map, and with Cursor bullseye the bearing and range from the bullseye. By finger it follows your last tap; on a phone a tap opens a second line.
PanelTab: The map's options, or the list of what your HSD will show.
Section/map: The map itself: style, label ink, landmarks, grid and bullseye.
Section/flightplan: Your flight plan, PPTs, lines and support tracks.
Section/package: The other flights of your package.
Section/intel: Air defences, search radars, JSTARS and units from the save.
Section/cheats: What BMS holds that your side has not seen.
OpenBank: Puts this point into STPT 81-99, the DTC page's Open 1 and Open 2 tabs: choose the slot and the steerpoint type. An airfield goes in as Land with its name and elevation (an alternate); a threat as Precision; anything else as Nav. On a phone, a long press on a field or threat in the list opens it directly.
OpenBankWhat: What goes in: the airfield under a right-click, or the exact point clicked.
OpenBankType: The steerpoint's type, as the Open tabs' Change window sets it. Land for an alternate, Precision for a target.
OpenBankMore: Every type the DTC's Change window offers.
OpenBankSlot: The slot it goes into, with what each slot holds now. An occupied slot is replaced only after a question.
OpenBankAdd: Places it on the DTC page as its own edit; Save to DTC writes it to the cartridge.
